outcome: Accuracy of the Grobman prediction nomogram in predicting VBAC success
cohort: 421 women with a singleton, cephalic pregnancy at term and one previous lower segment caesarean section in Northland, New Zealand
finding: The Grobman model showed reasonable accuracy in predicting successful VBAC in a New Zealand population, particularly for Māori and Pacifika women.
mod_finding: This study evaluated the Grobman prediction nomogram for predicting successful vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) in a New Zealand population and found that it performed reasonably well.
